input.summary:
Shell B (plots 4-7) builds clean: ./make.sh writes build.nbt with 1537 placed, 0 refused, and no off-palette blocks.
The only fix was the water x8 in the plot 6 water tank: the core cells (x80..81, z15..16, y6..7) are now full water_cauldron (level 3), placed before water_tank so its air-only writes skip them.
Edits are confined to parts/shell_b.mjs.
left: The tank core is a stack of two level-3 water cauldrons, the closest palette stand-in for water. It is visually approximate, not water.

vocab/h4.mjs water_tank still writes the water block into air. That is outside this part; if another part calls it without pre-filling the core, OFF-PALETTE water will return. Fixing it belongs to the vocab owner, or the palette should add water to the plan.

waste.what: Diagnosing the off-palette water: the report counts every write, including the water the vocab helper emits before any later overwrite, so an after-the-fact fix in the part still showed water x8. Found the cause only by reading runParts' accounting in build.mjs.
waste.cost: about 3 make.sh rebuilds plus reading build.mjs runParts (around 60 lines)
waste.tool: runParts' off-palette report could check the final block at each cell it wrote (or a dry-run mode that lists what a part would write), and the water_tank helper could take a core-block option (e.g. core: 'water_cauldron') or a palette check at call time.

waste.what: Working out the tank core coordinates by hand from the water_tank footprint (x0+1..x0+2, z0+1..z0+2, y+5..y+6).
waste.cost: a few reasoning steps, then one 8-cell loop
waste.tool: water_tank could return its core cell list, so a part can swap those cells without re-deriving the offsets.
